newsitem.title: MACAU: Portugeuse president confident about Macau.
newsitem.headline: Portugeuse president confident about Macau.

text.p: Portuguese President Jorge Sampaio travelled to China on Sunday after visiting Macau where he predicted a smooth transition of the tiny Portuguese-administered territory to Chinese rule.
Sampaio left for an eight-day stay in China after paying his first official visit to Macau.
There "exists no problem that cannot be resolved in this transition process" ahead of Macau's reversion to China in December 1999, he told a news conference on Saturday.

All the enclave's transitional problems, including those on citizens' rights, liberties and legal guarantees, could be resolved before the return based on "the respect for the Sino-Portuguese Joint Declaration", signed by the two countries in 1987, which governs the handover.
Beijing and Lisbon have described their relations over Macau as "excellent".

Macau will revert to China on December 20, 1999 after nearly 450 years of Portuguese administration. Like its neighbor, Hong Kong, which reverts to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30 this year, tiny Macau will become a Special Administrative Region of China.
Sampaio added he was confident that the local administration was able to fight crime.
"We have to fight all that is negative, we have to fight the things that disturb the transition period," he said.
Macau has been hit by a string of violent crimes since late 1995, including 14 home-made bomb attacks.
Police say most of the bombings are believed to be "acts of revenge" by rival organized crime gangs, called triads.
